name: Sun
description: The star at the center of our Solar System.

name: Mercury
description: The smallest planet in the Solar System.

name: BepiColombo
description: Joint ESA and JAXA mission to explore Mercury. Aims to map Mercury's surface at various wavelengths, map surface geology and composition, determine Mercury's core, and study Mercury's magnetic field and exosphere.
ou_involvement: OU Professors and Academics are a part of the M-CAM monitoring team, and have been a part of this since early planning in the 1990s. OU scientists contributed to the MIXS hardware. The OU is using the missions first images and data for teaching and PhD projects.

name: Venus
description: Second planet from the Sun.

name: Earth
description: Our home planet.

name: ISS
description: The International Space Station, a modular space station in low Earth orbit.
ou_involvement: Materials Science: The OU has flown experiments to expose materials to the harsh space environment.

name: Hubble
description: A legendary space telescope that has revolutionized astronomy.
ou_involvement: Detector Heritage: The CCD technology in WFC3 shares heritage with CEI-characterized sensors.  OU astronomers use Hubble data for both teaching and research in astronomy.

name: Sentinel-5P
description: TROPOMI (Tropospheric Monitoring Instrument) - A imaging spectrometer that measures atmospheric trace gases such as nitrogen dioxide (NO2), ozone (O3), methane (CH4), carbon monoxide (CO). Supporting air quality testing, cimate monitoring and environmental policy decisions.

name: Sentinel-2
description: For high-resolution optical imaging of the Earths land surfaces. This includes vegetation abundance, forests, soils, water and coastal areas. For environmental monitoring, disaster response and more.
ou_involvement: OU researches use Sentinel-2 data in scientific work, such as estimating soil moisture in advanced machine learning techniques, and studying forest fire evolution.

name: Sentinel-3
description: Provides high resolution, real-time data about oceans, land, ice and atmosphere for ocean forecasting and climate research. This includes ocean topography and wave measurements, ocean and land temperature fluctuations, and supporting marine ecosystem pollution.
ou_involvement: OU researchers use a combination of Sentinel-3 and Sentinel-2 data for modelling high-resolutioni evapotranspiration.

name: CASTOR
description: Cosmological Advanced Survey Telescope for Optical and UV Research (CASTOR). Wide-field, high resolution iaging in the UV and blue-optical wavelengths.
ou_involvement: The CEI at the OU recieved funding for the test and development of detectors optimised for space UV applications. This involved raising the Technology Readiness Level of these detectors.

name: TRUTHS
description: Traceable Radiometry Underpinning Terrestrial and Helio-Studies (TRUTHS). Planned Earth observation satellite led by the UKSA and delivered by ESA. Aims to measure incoming solar radiation and Earth-reflected radiation to establish calibration references for other satellites. Will improve confidence in climate measurements and improve confidence in long-term climate data.

name: SMILE
description: Solar wind Magnetosphere Ionosphere Link Explorer (SMILE). Space science mission studying the Sun-Earth connection. The interaction between solar wind and the Earths magnetosphere and ionosphere.
ou_involvement: Direct involvement with SMILE detector development and optimisation. The CEI are working on the CCDs to optimise performance and understand radiation defects to maximise scientific data return.

name: Swift
description: Originally mission duration was 2 years, but Swift is still operating 20+ years later. Swift detects and localises gamma ray bursts and relays positions of these for observational follow up. Contributes to transient astrophysics.
ou_involvement: OU scientists contributed to the BAT instrument, with calibration and science planning. The CEI expertise in detector calibration was applied in pre-launch testing.

name: UKube-1
description: A technology demonstration CubeSat for the testing of in-orbit small satellite technologies, and monitoring of space weather and radiation. Enabling education and capacity building for UK universities and industry. Serving as a waymaker for UK small satellite missions.
ou_involvement: The OU was invovled in payload and science planning, especially related to space environment and radiation measurements. OU researchers provided high-energy particle detection, supported data analysis, and the CEI contributed to the design and testing of detectors.

name: Chandrayaan-1
description: A series of lunar missions launched by ISRO to map and study the moon.
ou_involvement: The CEI at the OU completed radiation damage assessments and pre-flight characterisation of the X-ray detectors.

name: Chang'e-5
description: Lunar sample return mission. Samples returned to Earth 16 December 2020.
ou_involvement: OU Professor Mahesh Anad was selected as one of 7 scientists to receive moon samples. The team at the OU plan to determine the amount and isotopic composition of carbon, nitrogen, oxygen and noble gases in these samples. These results will evaluate the giant-impact origin of the Moon.

name: Luna 27
description: Planned Russian lunar lander mission. Aim to conduct in-situ scientific experiments on the lunar surface, in the south polar region, searching for volatiles in the permenantly shadowed areas of the Moon.
ou_involvement: The CEI at the OU is developing part of the PROSPECT package, a scientific laboratory to analyse luanr soil samples. OU scientists are building and testing this to operate in the lunar environment.

name: LUPEX
description: Joint lunar lander by ISRO and JAXA. Aim to explore the lunar south pole for water and othere researches in permenantly shadowed regions.
ou_involvement: Dr Simon Sheridan is teh science lead for developing the Exploration Mass Spectrometer for LUPEX. This will measure volitiles released from the luna sub-surface materials.

name: Earth-Sun L2
description: Lagrange Point 2

name: JWST
description: The James Webb Space Telescope (JWST. Hubble successor optimised for infrared astronomy. Aimed to observe first galaxies and stars, galaxy evolution, study of exoplanet atmospheres, and observe solar system objects.
ou_involvement: Many OU astronomers use JWST data in research. OU academics have contributed to JWST observation proposals, especially for exoplanet studies and infrared imaging of galaxies.

name: Gaia
description: GAIA aimed to produce a 3D map of the Milky Way to provide data on structure, formation and evolution. GAIA mapped the distances, motions, and brightness of ~1.8 billion stars in the Milky Way. GAIA detected binary systems, exoplanets and variable stars, and contributed to fundamental physics, including tests of general relativity.
ou_involvement: The CEI worked extensively on GAIA CCDs. This included modelling of radiation damage and charge transfer efficiency to establish performance predictions. After launch, CEI researchers looked at in-fight radiation damage. OU astronomers and PhD students actively use GAIA data for stellar and galactic studies.

name: Euclid
description: EUCLID is a major ESA mission designed to explore the Dark Universe - Dark matter and dark energy, by mapping the 3D structure of the cosmos. It observes billions of galaxies out to ~10 billion light years to track Universe expansion.
ou_involvement: The CEI played a direct role in EUCLID instrmentation. The CEI characterised the CCDs for the VIS instrument. This included experimental characterisation of CCDs and radiation effects for detector performance. The CEI developed 'Trap-Pumping' analysis which is now used in-orbit to calibrate and map radiation damage on the detectors.  OU astronomers analyse EUCLID survey data to identify gravitational lenses to trace dark matter distributions.

name: Athena
description: Advanced Telescope for High ENergy Astrophysics (ATHENA). Powerful X-ray space observatory to explore the hot and energetic Universe. Aims to t
ou_involvement: The CEI is leading the design and testing of graded-Z shielding for the WFI. This is essential for minimising background noise caused by high energy particles. The CEI is using simulations to model charged particle interactions to validate performance for ATHENA. OU astronomers are contributing to pre-mission planning on topics such as black hole growth, galaxy clusters and hot gas in the Universe.

name: HWO
description: Habitable Worlds Observatory (HWO). Planned next-generation flagship space telescope designed to search for life beyond our Solar System. It will directly image and characterise the atmospheres of Earth-like exoplanets. It is a successor to Hubble, JWST, and (once launched,) Roman, but built specifically to image Earth-like exoplanets.
ou_involvement: The CEI is very involved in the development of high precision, low-noise imaging detectors for photon counting regimes. CEI academics are a part of the HWO development group, working on technology development proposals and leading UKSA involvement.

name: PLATO
description: PLAnetary Transits and Oscillations of stars (PLATO). Aim to detect terrestrial exoplanets around bright, nearby stars, especially in the habitable zone.
ou_involvement: OU astronomers and CEI researchers are a part of the PLATO Science Team. They contribute to detector performance studies, calibration, and radiation tolerance simulations.

name: Roman
description: Roman aims to study dark energy via galaxy surveys and supernova observations, directly image exoplanets, and conduct wide-field infrared surveys of the Universe. Romans CGI is a technology demonstration to demonstrate direct imaging of exoplanets and raise the TRL of active CGI optics and EM-CCD technology. This will directly inform the development of HWO.
ou_involvement: CEI academics have been heavily involved in the testing and modification of EM-CCDs for use on Roman. Significant testing of the baseline detector informed radiation hard, modified EM-CCDs, and developed the flight device. CEI involvement will continue as Roman will use in-orbit Trap-Pumping, much like EUCLID. OU astronomers will use Roman data for microlensing studies, dark energy research, and stellar population studies.

name: Mars
description: The Red Planet.

name: ExoMars TGO
description: ExoMars Trace Gas Orbiter. Detect and map trace gases in the Martian atmosphere - particularly methane - to identify possible biological or geological sources. Studies the atmospheres composition, structure and variability. Serves as a communications relay for surface missions such as the ExoMars Rover.
ou_involvement: The CEI leads the NOMAD instrument that analyses infrared and UV for atmosphereic trace gas detection. OU researches actively analyse TGO data, focussing on methane detection, understanding seasonal and spatial variation of trace gases, contributing to broader Mars atmospheric science. OU scientists collaborate internationally on data validation and instrument comparison.

name: Beagle 2
description: Mars Lander - failed to fully deploy. Partial contact confirmed in 2015. Aimed to search for signs of past life on Mars via organic molecule detection.
ou_involvement: OU scientists built GAP: Designed and built the Gas Analysis Package (mass spectrometer & oven) to analyse soil. OU scientific involvement in pre-launch mission simulations were later used to inform planetary lander missions, including ExoMars.

name: Perseverance
description: Mars Perseverence Rover. Aims to search for signs of ancient microbial life in the Jezero Crater. Collecting rock and soil samples for a potential Earth sample return. Demonstrating new technologies for Mars missions.
ou_involvement: OU researchers actively use data from Perserverance for: remote sensing and geology studies, martian surface composition and climate analysis, and planetary science OU academics use mission data for teaching.

name: ExoMars Rosalind Franklin
description: Mars Rover to search for signs of past or present life in the Martian subsurface. Will drill up to 2 metres to access protected samples. Aims to analys geology, mineralogy, and geochemistry.
ou_involvement: The CEI has been invovled in detector development for this mission, supporting CCD/CMOS detector characterisation for spectrometers and imaging systems. OU astronomers and minierologists are developing data analysis pipelines and data planning models

name: MSL Curiosity
description: Mars Rover to assess Mars past and present habitability. Aims to characterise geology, mineralogy and climate.
ou_involvement: Some OU academics are directly participating and informing Curiosity Science. Dr Susanne Schwenzer - focus on understanding Martian chemistries relating to habitability, including noble gas studies. Dr James Holmes - Postdoctoral researcher, focussing on Mars atmospheric chemistry cycles using observations and modelling. There are many other OU academics using Curiosity data to inform research projects.

name: Jupiter
description: The largest planet.

name: JUICE
description: JUpiter ICy moons Explorer. Characterising Jupiters icy moons, focussing on Ganymede, Europa, and Callisto.
ou_involvement: Sensor Validation: The CEI validated CMOS sensors for the JANUS camera system using data from UKube-1. OU planetary scientists participate in science planning, modelling, and mission simulations.

name: Saturn
description: Famous for its rings.

name: Cassini
description: The mission that revolutionized our understanding of the Saturnian system. Studied Saturns atmosphere, rings, and magnetosphere. Explored Titan an Enceladus, including surface composition. Delivered the Huygens probe to Titan.
ou_involvement: OU planetary scientists used Cassini data extensivley for reasearch on: Saturns rings and moons, habitability and cryovolcanism on Enceladus, and planetary magnetosphers of Saturn.

name: Huygens
description: Huygens Probe - Part of Cassini. The first and only landing in the outer solar system. Aimed to perform in situ analysis of Titans atmosphere and surface.
ou_involvement: OU scientists were involved in the planning and data interpretation of Huygens instruments. OU planetary scientists contributed to post-landing data analysis for atmospheric and surface studies.

name: Rosetta
description: Comet rendezvous and lander mission. To study comet 67P in detail- including composition, structure, and activity.
ou_involvement: OU scientists were actively involved in Rosetta science planning and data analysis. Particularly: Imaging and spectroscopy analysis, comet surface morphology, plasma interactions and comet environments.

name: Philae
description: The lander from the Rosetta Mission.

name: Hera
description: To study the effects of the DART spacecraft kinetic impact on Dimorphos. To characterise the internal structure, composition, and surface properties of Didymos and Dimorphos. Aims to provide detailed measurements of asteroid dynamics.
ou_involvement: OU researchers involved in pre-launch mission simulations, and performance modelling.

name: AKARI
description: Japanese infrared astronomy satellite that surveyed the entire sky.
ou_involvement: OU researchers used AKARI data to study interstellar dust and star formation.

name: Spitzer
description: Infrared Great Observatory that discovered the 'TRAPPIST-1' exoplanets.
ou_involvement: Exoplanets: OU scientists analyze Spitzer light curves to characterize exoplanet atmospheres.

name: Herschel
description: The largest infrared telescope ever flown; studied the coolest objects in the universe.
ou_involvement: SPIRE Instrument: The OU was a co-investigator institute for the SPIRE camera/spectrometer.

name: Planck
description: Mapped the Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB) with unprecedented precision.
ou_involvement: OU researchers used Planck data to study galaxy clusters and the early universe structure.

name: Peregrine
description: First private US lunar lander (Astrobotic). It suffered a propellant leak and re-entered Earth's atmosphere.
ou_involvement: The OU developed the Exospheric Mass Spectrometer (PITMS) to measure the lunar exosphere.

name: Comet Interceptor
description: A mission to ambush a pristine, long-period comet entering the inner solar system for the first time.
ou_involvement: Instruments: The OU is providing the focal plane arrays for the Modular X-ray Source (MIXS) heritage instrument.

name: EnVision
description: ESA orbiter to study Venus' geology, surface composition and atmosphere.
ou_involvement: The CEI is helping design and characterise UV detectors for the spectrometer on EnVision. Dr Manish Patel leads the space research team, which is involved in science preparation and future data collection planning.

name: OGRE
description: Off-plane Grating Rocket Experiment. A sub-orbital sounding rocket to capture the highest resolution soft X-ray spectrum of Capella.
ou_involvement: The CEI developed the EMCCD camera system to survive the violent vibration of a rocket launch.

name: Hayabusa2
description: Japanese mission that deploy rovers and returned samples from Ryugu.
ou_involvement: Sample Analysis: OU researchers analyzed the returned Ryugu grains to study water and organics.

name: OSIRIS-REx
description: Returned a massive sample from asteroid Bennu; now renamed OSIRIS-APEX to study Apophis.
ou_involvement: The OU is analyzing the Bennu samples to investigate the early solar system's chemistry.

name: Stardust
description: The first mission to return cometary dust (from Comet Wild 2) to Earth.
ou_involvement: Sample Analysis: The OU led the analysis of the cometary dust tracks in the aerogel collector.

name: Bennu
description: A carbonaceous, diamond-shaped near-Earth asteroid.

name: Ryugu
description: A diamond-shaped near-Earth asteroid sampled by Hayabusa2.

name: Comet Wild 2
description: A lumpy comet visited by Stardust in 2004.

name: Earth-Sun L1
description: Lagrange Point 1

name: Genesis
description: Collected solar wind samples. The return capsule crash-landed in Utah, but the samples were successfully recovered.
ou_involvement: Oxygen Isotopes: OU researchers used the NanoSIMS to analyze the returned samples, revealing the Sun's oxygen isotopic composition.
